comments.author: jameskilton
comments.story: Rails, callbacks, workers, and the race you never expected to lose
comments.why: Hexagonal architecture to avoid callback interdependencies.
comments.text: Was going to say the same thing. Models should not know or care about background queues or mailings, and callback use has always caused problems for me later on. Nothing against the OP, it does explain a common edge case that many people will run into and for that it's a good article, but I wish more people would see the violations of SRP going on here and try to lead people away from this trap. I'd recommend watching [VIDEO] (Hexagonal Rails GoRuCo talk) for one way to re-architect to get away from these inter dependencies.

comments.author: douglasfshearer
comments.why: Hexagonal Rails talk cited among sources for thin-model, service-layer style
comments.text: Rails used as intended can be a real pain to upgrade, I agree. Recently I have been developing applications in the "thin-model, thin-controller, with a service layer and external API wrappers" style, as espoused by Gary Bernhardt [1] and others [2] [3] [4] [5]. I upgraded to the latest Rails this morning on one app, and apart from swapping the Money gem to use the git repository, until they have a new version out with compatible dependency, it went smoothly. All the specs and acceptance tests passing with no alteration required. [1] [LINK] [2] [LINK] [3] [LINK] [4] [LINK] [5] [VIDEO]

comments.author: kentwistle
comments.why: Hexagonal Rails as a decoupling resource.
comments.text: Am I only the only one that doesn't find 'All tests in 4 minutes, all model tests in 80 seconds' very impressive? It sounds like a really long time to me. You know what could increase the speed dramatically.... decoupling. I also think decoupling phrased in the context of the Rails 2 to Rails 3 upgrade, where pretty much everything changed, makes perfect sense. Imagine just having a few wrapper classes that spoke to Rails and only having to adapt them. Sounds good to me! Bernhardt: Boundaries [LINK] Weirich: Decoupling from Rails [LINK] Wynne: Hexagonal Rails [VIDEO]
